entries.claim: Task 6 says a heading idSections rejects names no epic, so a dependency on it fails. That breaks the existing 'a tagged epic heading' case in tests/check.test.mjs:132-133, and it breaks Task 6's own no-double-report intent, because one root cause now produces two lines. The task gives no instruction for this conflict.
entries.failure_scenario: The existing case tags E-01's heading ('## E-01: Catalog [ASSUMPTION]'). idSections rejects that heading (lib/check.mjs:111, 118-119), so E-01 drops out of the accepted epic order. E-02's '**Depends on:** E-01' then hits Task 6's 'an ID no epic in the file has' branch. checkDir returns two lines: the heading problem plus 'epics.md: E-02: Depends on: "E-01" ...'. The case expects only ['epics.md: "## E-01: Catalog [ASSUMPTION]": not a "## E-01: name" heading'], so it fails and Task 6 verify (1) (`node --test tests/*.test.mjs`) goes red. The executor must then choose between rewriting a pinned expectation so one tagged heading reports twice, or departing from the plan's stated rule (for example, treating a rejected heading's ID as known). The plan does not settle which.

entries.claim: Task 3 writes the only worked epics example in SKILL.md before Task 4 adds the build-order and citation rules (D-06, D-09, D-07). Task 3 names only D-02, D-03 and D-05, and Task 4 neither brings that example in line with its rules nor checks it, so the shipped example can contradict the locked D-09 citation rule.
entries.failure_scenario: The Task 3 executor builds the example on Gristmill as suggested. That spine has S-01 (how state changes) and S-02 (design approach). If the executor follows the FORMAT.md Tally template, whose E-01 has `**Spine decisions:** None`, the result is a Gristmill E-01 with `None`, or one citing only S-01. Task 4 then adds 'Every epic cites every design approach, stack and hosting decision' to section 19. Its verify only greps the section for 'MVP', 'hosting' and 'design approach' and a sentence about citing every S- ID, so it passes, and SKILL.md ships an example that breaks its own D-09 rule. A run that copies the example's citation pattern then fails Plan 4's every-epic-cites-project-wide grader (every epic must cite S-02, S-04 and S-05), and success criterion 2's citation proof fails on the step's text, not on the model.

entries.claim: Task 3 says "Go on from the brief" "gains two branches" but never removes or rewrites the existing three-document branch at SKILL.md line 181 ("A brief, a PRD and a spine: write nothing, and end on the later-release line"). Line 123 even says every remaining mention of the later-release line now means the new one, and Verify (3) only checks that the two new branches are present.
entries.failure_scenario: An executor follows the text literally and adds the two new branches next to line 181. Verify (1) through (5) all pass, because line 181 doesn't contain the retired sentence and the new branches are present. A user then has a brief, a PRD and a spine but no epics, gives non-empty text, and answers "go on" at the documents question. The first matching branch, "A brief, a PRD and a spine", ends on the new later-release line instead of the epics resume line and the epics step. That breaks the must-be-true "Going on from the documents question takes the same branches" and D-16. No case in Plans 4 to 6 exercises the go-on answer, so nothing catches it.

entries.claim: Verify (6)'s fallback lets the size check pass on Verify (7) alone, but architecture-on-request cannot detect a cut in SKILL.md's last section. The plan's must-be-true that a kept trace shows SKILL.md loaded through its last section can therefore be reported done while it is false, and the flagged 'Unclear' truncation assumption that Plans 2 and 3 hand to this plan stays open.
entries.failure_scenario: The kept epics-from-spine trace holds no copy of the skill body (the plan allows this branch at line 123), so Verify (6) says so and relies on (7). architecture-on-request's only grader is evals/architecture-on-request/graders/writes-architecture.md, a file_exists check. Earlier parts of SKILL.md already tell the model that `/seldon architecture` writes `.planning/seldon/architecture.md`: the frontmatter description at line 3, `<rules>` at lines 30-31 and the section 1 route at lines 55 and 65. So if the loader cuts the file inside '21. The architecture document', which holds the rules against new decisions and own IDs and the ending without a question, the model still writes architecture.md, the case scores 1.00, and the plan records SKILL.md's size as safe. The must-be-true at line 54 is then untrue, and nothing in Verify (5) to (7) catches it.

entries.claim: The split fixture puts the first four requirements on one side and the last four on the other, so the boundary falls exactly where an even split by count would fall. The epics-split case therefore cannot tell a split along the boundary from a split into equal halves by count, and it can score 1.00 while success criterion 3's "split along a spine boundary" fails.
entries.failure_scenario: Take an epics step that ignores the boundary's text and cuts the 8-requirement category into two equal halves in PRD order (IDs 1-4, then 5-8). It cites the spine's only `Kind: boundaries` decision on both epics, which D-07 and D-09 tell it to do anyway. The resulting epics.md passes every grader. `splits-category` sees two lines, one with each side's IDs. `no-mixed-epic` finds no line with IDs from both sides, because the halves are the sides. `at-most-five-ids`, `at-most-five-done-when` and `both-halves-cite-boundary` all pass, and `--epics` exits 0. The case scores 1.00. Verify (3) and the Notes (line 143) only show that a first-five count split fails. The other natural count split, equal halves, is never ruled out. D-21 names only the first-five split, so the plan meets the letter of D-21. But the fixture shape is the planner's own choice, and that choice leaves 'along the boundary' unproven. Two shapes would fix it: sides interleaved in PRD order, or an uneven contiguous split such as 3 and 5 with the NFR on the 3 side. Either one fails both count splits.

entries.claim: The retired-line grep in must-be-true 5 and Task 3 Verify (6) only comes out right under Claude Code's `grep`, which is a shell function running ugrep with `--ignore-files` (skips gitignored files). Plain GNU grep reads the gitignored `evals/results/` folders and the replay session files beside each `history.jsonl`, and both already hold the old line.
entries.failure_scenario: I ran `command grep -rn 'The epics step comes in a later release' skills/ docs/ README.md evals/` on today's tree. Besides the three tracked hits it prints dozens more: `evals/results/2026-11-17T18-25-55-143Z/aggregate-result.json`, the `report.html` files, and `evals/spine-job/2414dea2-...jsonl` plus about a dozen other `<uuid>.jsonl` session files. Those files are ignored by `evals/.gitignore` and neither Plan 6 nor Plan 7 removes them. After Task 3 is correct, a verifier or a UAT run in an ordinary terminal still gets output, so 'prints nothing' fails and AC5's grep reads as failed. Verify (6)'s claim that before the task the grep prints only the line in `evals/resume-later/graders/says-later-release.md` is also false under plain grep. Only the Claude Code wrapper gives the stated results. Running `git grep` instead would make the check depend on tracked files only.

entries.claim: `ends-on-confirm.md` requires the word `confirm` on the last non-blank line. SKILL.md fixes no words for that question: Plan 3 Task 1 and 'The check' (SKILL.md 503-506) only say 'one plain-prose question asking whether the user confirms'. That breaks the plan's own rule (Context line 59, Plans 2 and 3) that every line a grader matches is copied from SKILL.md.
entries.failure_scenario: The full-walk run follows SKILL.md correctly: it says the resume line, writes `epics.md`, repeats `seldon check: epics.md conforms`, then ends on 'Do these epics look right, or do you want changes?'. That is a valid plain-prose confirm question, but it does not contain `confirm`. `ends-on-confirm` fails, full-walk scores below 1.00 and Verify (5) fails on a correct run. The executor then has to change SKILL.md under the lease, or loosen the grader, to fix a defect in the grader rather than in the skill. Task 1's D-21 checks (3) include only negative cases for this grader, so nothing ties its pattern to wording SKILL.md fixes.

entries.claim: Task 2 check (5) runs `grep -rn 'The epics step comes in a later release' ... evals/`, and that recursive grep also reads the git-ignored `evals/results/` folder, where earlier phase 4 runs left the retired line on disk, so the check fails even when every tracked file is correct.
entries.failure_scenario: Today `grep -rl 'The epics step comes in a later release' evals/` finds 6 files under `evals/results/` (aggregate-result.json and report.html in 2026-11-17T18-25-55-143Z, 2026-11-17T18-26-30-521Z and 2026-11-17T19-13-10-936Z). `evals/.gitignore` ignores `results/`, but plain `grep -rn` doesn't honor that. Plans 3, 4 and 6 can remove the line from SKILL.md and both graders, and README.md can be fixed too, and check (5) still prints those 6 hits and fails. The executor then has two choices. It can raise a false checkpoint, or it can delete local run results to make the check pass, which is not in the plan and not in its README.md-only lease. Nothing in the plan scopes the grep to tracked files (for example `git grep`, or `--exclude-dir=results`) or says what to do with old results.
